title: prompt-library-scratchpad-talia-chen
content:
OBJECTIVE:
- Build a small set of reusable prompt templates and few-shot examples for the prompt library. Focus on: structured extraction (JSON), safe chat completions, and short-answer summarization for product docs. Keep prompts robust to model variation (gpt-style and open weights).

CURRENT NOTES / HYPOTHESES:
- Templates should include: 1) explicit output schema, 2) examples showing edge-cases (missing fields, contradictory input), 3) a short instruction + a strict formatting line.
- Few-shot examples: 3-5 per template is a good balance — enough to show pattern, not so many that prompt size explodes.
- Failure modes to capture: hallucinated facts, truncated output, inconsistent key naming, mixing levels of detail.

TEMPLATE A: JSON-EXTRACT (product-feature extractor)
- Use case: From a product spec paragraph, extract fields: name, short_description, target_user, constraints (list), key_metrics (list), examples (list).
- Prompt skeleton (short):
  "You are a JSON extractor. Given the product note below, output valid JSON with keys: name, short_description, target_user, constraints, key_metrics, examples. If a field is not present, use an empty string or empty list. Do NOT include any extra keys. Always return only JSON, nothing else."

FEW-SHOT SET (3 examples)
1) Input: "New feature: QuickShare lets users share docs in 2 clicks and expire links. Ideal for enterprise admins who need audit logs."
   Output: {"name":"QuickShare","short_description":"Share docs in 2 clicks with expiring links","target_user":"enterprise admins","constraints":["audit logging required"],"key_metrics":["share_time","link_expiration_rate"],"examples":[]}

2) Input: "Beta: SmartAssist autofills help-center answers. Not for regulatory content. Works for FAQ and troubleshooting."
   Output: {"name":"SmartAssist","short_description":"Autofills help-center answers for FAQs and troubleshooting","target_user":"support agents","constraints":["not for regulatory content"],"key_metrics":["answer_accuracy","resolution_time"],"examples":[]}

3) Input: "Idea: Offline Mode caches key assets. For mobile users with intermittent connectivity. Cache size configurable."
   Output: {"name":"Offline Mode","short_description":"Caches key assets for offline access","target_user":"mobile users","constraints":["configurable cache size"],"key_metrics":["cache_hit_rate","sync_time"],"examples":[]}

PROMPT TUNING NOTES (A):
- Add a "STRICT_JSON_ONLY" line after instructions to reduce preamble.
- For open models that sometimes prepend commentary, include an explicit: "Do not prepend any commentary or apologies. Output must start with '{'".
- If model often uses single quotes, add: "Use double quotes for strings".

TEMPLATE B: SAFE-CHAT + TOOL-CALLS (dialogue assistant that can call tools)
- Use case: Assistants that propose calling a search tool or a calculation tool. Must explicitly mark tool_call object when needed.
- Instruction pattern:
  "You are an assistant that can call tools. Decide whether to call a tool. If calling, return JSON: {\"action\": \"tool_call\", \"tool\": \"<tool_name>\", \"input\": {...}}. If not, return {\"action\": \"respond\", \"content\": \"<final answer>\"}. Always return valid JSON only."

FEW-SHOT (2 positive, 1 negative case)
- Pos1: User asks for latest compliance policy -> tool_call: search_policy with input {query: 'compliance policy 2026'}
- Pos2: User asks to calculate ROI -> tool_call: calculator with input {numbers...}
- Neg: User asks for general advice -> respond with content string (no tool_call).

FAILURE CASES (B):
- Model returns text + JSON. Fix: add "ONLY_RETURN_JSON" strong line.
- Model invents a tool that doesn't exist. Fix: enumerate allowed tools in prompt.

TEMPLATE C: SHORT_SUMMARY (3-sentence limit)
- Task: Given a meeting note, produce a 3-sentence summary with one action item.
- Instruction: "Produce at most 3 sentences. End with 'Action: <who> - <task>' if there is an action. If none, end with 'Action: none'"

FEW-SHOT EXAMPLE:
- Input: "Spent time reviewing scope; agreed on timeline; Bob to prototype UI by next week; need legal review."
  Output: "Team agreed on timeline and scope; Bob will prototype the UI; legal review required. Action: Bob - build prototype by next week"

EXPERIMENT LOG (quick):
- 2025-12-05: Ran A on model-open-v1 (quantized) -> 82% valid JSON, ~5% extra text, common miss: key_metrics sometimes merged into string.
- 2026-01-10: Added 'Use double quotes' line -> valid JSON increased to 91%.
- 2026-01-22: Added explicit empty-list rule -> fewer missing keys, but slight increase in hallucinated metric names.
- 2026-02-02: For B, enumerated tools -> model attempted only listed tools. Still prefixed with "Note:" occasionally.

FAILURE / EDGE CASES I WANT TO COVER IN TEST SUITE:
- Ambiguous referent: "it" referencing multiple products in paragraph -> extractor should prefer most recent noun or return empty for name and include context? (decide)
- Conflicting metrics mentioned: If both "latency" and "response_time" used, normalize to key_metrics entries with original text and also add a normalized tag? For now, keep original strings.
- Lots of bullets: long lists should truncate to top 5 items (note: set explicit instruction).
- Non-English phrases present: ensure language detection step or leave verbatim.

EVALUATION METRIC IDEAS:
- Strict JSON validity (parser check) -> binary
- Schema coverage: percent of required fields populated (empty allowed but present)
- Key-name consistency (map to canonical names) -> fuzzy string match metric
- Hallucination check: compare extracted facts to source facts via string containment / fuzzy matching
- Robustness to adversarial phrasing: test set with rhetorical questions and ironic phrasing

QUICK TODOs / NEXT STEPS:
- [ ] Add normalization map for common synonyms (latency -> response_time) into library metadata (confluence:DEVEX-PROMPT-LIB).
- [ ] Convert A into two variants: strict-schema (for ingestion pipeline) and tolerant (for UI preview).
- [ ] Create 30 curated evals covering: missing fields, ambiguous referents, contradicting statements, nested product combos.
- [ ] Run batch eval across open-v* + gpt-like API and log per-model failure reasons (Jira INF-987).

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF:
- Should we allow the extractor to merge repeated fields into arrays or prefer first occurence? Leaning to arrays for metrics/constraints.
- For tool-calling, how do we surface the tool confidence? Maybe add a top-level score field for tool_call decisions. Needs platform support.
- Conversation context length: when past context > 2k tokens, prefer sparse examples (1-shot) and rely on schema enforcement to preserve behavior.

SNIPPETS & PROMPT-LIB FORMAT IDEA (metadata)
- Each prompt artifact: id, name, purpose, input_schema, output_schema, examples (list), recommended_models, tags. (Will implement as metadata file in library).

MISC / RANDOM NOTES (scratch):
- Keep prompts < 2k tokens for hosted API to avoid cost blowup. Use templating to swap examples in/out.
- Consider adding a "sanity-check" post-process that validates JSON and tries to auto-repair common issues (single->double quotes, trailing commas, missing top-level braces).

REFERENCES/LINKS:
- Confluence page: confluence:DEVEX-PROMPT-LIB
- Jira ticket for eval harness: jira:INF-987
- Draft PR: github:github.com/redwood-inference/prompts/pull/42

END
